Horse to Zebra

Unpaired image-to-image translation. The model never saw a horse and a zebra in the same scene, yet it learned to swap one for the other.

  • CycleGAN
  • TensorFlow / Keras
  • Horse2Zebra
  • 100 epochs
Generated image from training checkpoint
Direction
  • 100epochs, about 16 hours on a T4 GPU
  • 2,401unpaired training photos
  • 256 x 256pixels per image
  • 4 networks2 generators, 2 discriminators

The idea: translate, then translate back

Without matched pairs there is no answer key. CycleGAN's trick is a round trip: turn a horse into a zebra, then turn that zebra back into a horse. If the result matches the starting photo, the translation kept the content and only changed the species. Pick a loss to see which parts of the diagram it trains.

How training went

Honest results

What works

  • Clear animals in simple scenes, like the grazing and beach horses.
  • Zebra to horse on the enclosure zebra, where the coat turns a convincing brown.

What doesn't

  • Distant herds and the close-up horse head: use the epoch buttons to see how they changed between 66 and 100. A later epoch is not always a better one in a GAN.
  • Zebra to horse often leaves a faint stripe texture.

Model details

Generators
ResNet: 7x7 conv, two downsamples, 9 residual blocks, two upsamples, tanh output. Instance norm and reflection padding.
Discriminators
70 x 70 PatchGAN. It scores overlapping patches instead of the whole image.
Losses
Least-squares adversarial, cycle weight 10, identity weight 5.
Optimizer
Adam, learning rate 2e-4, beta1 0.5, batch size 1.
Data
Horse2Zebra: 1,067 horse and 1,334 zebra training photos, 256 x 256. Random crop and flip during training.
Training
1,067 steps per epoch, 100 epochs, two sessions (epochs 1 to 66, then 67 to 100).
